title: [Bug]: UDM answers 404 "Not found" when its UE context pool is exhausted
body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0-205-g2c80f8f (tested); same code on main 51ee7ca (2026-10-26)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Keep the default `global.max.ue` (1024).
2. Provision more than 1024 subscribers and drive authentication or SDM requests for more than 1024 distinct SUPIs at the UDM (we used a Diameter-to-SBA interworking function issuing Nudm_SDM GET am-data and Nudm_UEAU generate-auth-data for 50,000 IMSIs).
3. After about 1022 distinct SUPIs, every request for a new SUPI fails.

### Logs

The UDM logs `No memory pool [<suci/supi>]` (`src/udm/context.c`), then `Invalid Request [...]` and `Not found [<method>]` (`src/udm/udm-sm.c`), and answers 404 "Not found" to every request for a SUPI it has no context for yet. Raising `global.max.ue` to 60000 made the same 50,000-subscriber run pass.

### Expected behaviour

A resource shortage in the UDM is a transient server-side condition. TS 29.500 clause 5.2.7.2 lists 500 INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES and 503 for this; a consumer then retries later or elsewhere.

### Observed Behaviour

The UDM answers 404 "Not found" (`src/udm/udm-sm.c`, `udm_ue_add()` failure falls into the generic `if (!udm_ue)` branch). A 404 on these resources means the subscriber does not exist, so consumers treat it as permanent: an AUSF/AMF rejects the UE, and an IMS interworking function maps it to DIAMETER_ERROR_USER_UNKNOWN (5001), after which the IMS stops retrying. The subscribers exist; only the pool is full.

Code at main 51ee7ca:
- `src/udm/context.c` L158: `ogs_error("No memory pool [%s]", suci);` → `udm_ue_add()` returns NULL
- `src/udm/udm-sm.c` L193–202: NULL from `udm_ue_add()` → `OGS_SBI_HTTP_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`

A possible fix is to distinguish the two cases in `udm-sm.c`: lookup miss stays 404, allocation failure answers 500 with cause INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES (or 503).

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not involved (UDM SBI only).

### UE Models and versions

Not involved; requests come from an SBA consumer.
